getting-started.title: Getting started
getting-started.summary: OneWebDev is a developer toolkit: data conversion, media processing, and Website Builder for building websites. Most tools run directly in your browser.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: The app has three sidebar menus: **Data**, **Media**, and **Website Builder**, plus the **Credits** and **Documentation** pages.
items: **Data** — Excel → JSON, Excel/JSON → SQL, Developer Utilities, and Server Conversion.
**Media** — image conversion, color picking, background removal, upscaling, metadata removal, plus video and audio tools.
**Website Builder** — Page Designer, Build Full Website, Website Templates, and Global Settings.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Pick a tool from the sidebar or from a card on the Dashboard.
Press the **Help** button in the page header to open a short guide for that tool without leaving the page.
Page addresses start with a language code (`/id/...` or `/en/...`); switch language any time from the header.
Menu items marked **Uses credits** include features that are processed on a server.

sections.heading: Where your data is processed
items: **Browser tools** (free): files are processed on your device and are never sent to a server.
**Server features** (credits): a file is only sent after you press the run button and accept the cost estimate.
Page Maker designs, website folders, icons, and fonts are stored in this browser's storage — not in an online account.

sections.heading: Limits & credit rules
items: Tools that run in the browser are always free.
Free in Website Builder: **2** website folders, up to **10** saved page designs, and **20** code exports.
Server features, premium templates, and premium items use credits. See the **Credits** topic.

pairs.a: That feature needs a server service that has not been enabled. No file is sent and no credits are charged. Use browser mode if it is available.

pairs.q: My designs or icons are missing on another device.
pairs.a: Website Builder data is stored per browser. Use the same browser and device, and do not clear site data.

sections.heading: Requires the backend
sections.body: Credit purchases, balance, transaction history, Media & Data server features, and premium item unlocks only work once the backend is configured. Without it, the app shows an honest "not available" notice and never creates fake transactions.

credits.title: Credits & payments
credits.summary: One credit balance for every paid feature: Media & Data server features, premium templates, and premium Website Builder items. Balance and access only change after the server confirms.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: The **Credits** page shows your balance, credit packages, Website Builder feature costs, server feature rates, a usage calculator, and transaction history.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Choose a package and press **Buy**. Payment happens on the payment provider's page; card or bank details never pass through this app.
When you return from checkout, the status is verified with the server. URL parameters are never treated as proof of payment.
Media & Data server features use the monthly quota of your **Plan** (there is a Free plan). VR panorama is still paid from the balance.
One-time items (templates, presets, elements, events, website slots) are unlocked from the credit dialog with the **Use** button.

sections.heading: Packages & costs
sections.body: All prices are in **Indonesian Rupiah**; 1 credit = Rp1,000 (base price). The amount charged always comes from the backend.
items: Packages: 20 credits = Rp20,000 · 50 = Rp47,500 · 100 = Rp90,000 · 250 = Rp212,500 · 500 = Rp400,000. Bigger packages cost less per credit (down to Rp800/credit).

Website Builder: code export after the 20 free ones **5** credits · extra website slot **15** · premium preset **5–10** · premium element **5–10** · premium event **5** · premium template **20–160** (one-time unlock) · 360° Tour Pro **50**.
Server features are charged per use (see the Media and Server Conversion topics).

sections.heading: Limits & credit rules
items: No fake transactions: balance, payments, and access only come from server responses.
Credits are only deducted after the server reports the job **succeeded**. Failed or cancelled = free.
Double clicks and repeated requests carry an idempotency key so you are not charged twice.
Items you already own are not charged again.
Checks in the browser are for convenience only; the backend enforces the real limits and balance.

pairs.a: The billing backend is not connected. No transaction was created and the balance did not change.

pairs.q: Asked to sign in to buy or use credits.
pairs.a: The server requires a signed-in session (cookie). Sign in through the backend account service and try again.
The balance increases once the payment provider confirms to the server. Press **Refresh** again shortly.
Buy a credit package on the **Credits** page, then repeat the action.

sections.heading: How credits work
sections.body: Balance, prices, and entitlements are always read from the server. The app keeps no API keys or secrets in the browser.
items: Payments are processed by Midtrans. A payment counts as paid only from a Midtrans notification with a valid signature, never from the page address.
Purchases and usage use idempotency keys, so a double click is never charged twice.
Admin accounts that passed 2FA use every feature without spending credits. Their usage is still logged for audit.
Purchase, usage, and refund history is on the **Credits** page.

data-excel-json.title: Excel → JSON
data-excel-json.summary: Turn Excel sheets (.xlsx/.xlsm) or CSV/TSV into JSON or a JavaScript module. Free and fully in the browser.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Converts many files at once, lets you pick a sheet per file, then download results one by one or as a ZIP. Files are never sent to a server.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Drop files on the upload area or click to choose them.
Set **Output options**: JSON or **JS module (.js)**, **First row as column names**, and **Pretty print (indent)**. Option changes apply to all results immediately.
Pick another sheet from the file card's sheet list if needed.
Press **Download** per file or **Download ZIP** for all results.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Input: `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`.
Output: `.json` (array of objects, or array of arrays when column names are off) or `.js` with `export default data`.
CSV is read as plain text (`007` stays `007`); `,` `;` tab or `|` delimiters are detected automatically; non-UTF-8 text is read as Windows-1252.
Dates become ISO text, formulas use their stored result, duplicate column names get a `_2` suffix.

sections.heading: Limits & credit rules
items: Max. **20 MB** per file and **30** files at a time.
Free, no credits.
Legacy `.xls`, `.ods`, `.xlsb`, `.numbers` formats cannot be read in the browser.

pairs.a: Re-save it as .xlsx or .csv, or press **Open Server Conversion** (uses credits) for .xls/.ods/.xlsb.

pairs.q: "This is not a modern Excel (.xlsx) file"
pairs.a: Probably a renamed .xls or a damaged file. Open it in Excel and save as .xlsx.

pairs.q: The Excel file is corrupt or password-protected.
pairs.a: Remove the password protection and save again.
Check the message above the list: unsupported format, over 20 MB, or more than 30 files.

data-sql.title: Excel/JSON → SQL
data-sql.summary: Generate ready-to-run INSERT INTO queries from Excel/CSV or JSON, with column mapping and database dialects. Free, in the browser.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: Turns data rows into `INSERT` statements for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, or generic (ANSI) SQL. Data is never sent to a server.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Choose a source: an Excel/CSV file, or JSON (paste text or **Open .json file**).
Fill in **Table name**, then set each column: include/exclude it and rename the database column.
Choose the **INSERT style** (**One INSERT, many rows** or **One INSERT per row**), **SQL dialect**, and **Empty values become NULL**.
The preview shows part of the rows; **Copy all** and the `.sql` download contain all data.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Excel/CSV input is the same as Excel → JSON (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`, max. 20 MB).
JSON input: an array of objects (or array of arrays → columns `kolom_1`, `kolom_2`, …); `.json` files max. 10 MB.
Identifiers are quoted per dialect: MySQL with backticks, PostgreSQL `"x"`, SQL Server `[x]`; generic stays unquoted when safe.
Booleans: `TRUE`/`FALSE` for PostgreSQL & generic, `1`/`0` for MySQL & SQL Server. Unicode text on SQL Server uses `N'...'`; MySQL backslashes are escaped.

sections.heading: Limits & credit rules
items: Free, no credits.
Column types (Number/Boolean/JSON/Text) are detected from the first 200 non-empty values; mixed values count as Text.
This tool only generates SQL text; it does not connect to your database.

sections.heading: Examples
items: Many-rows mode: `INSERT INTO "products" ("name", "price") VALUES ('Coffee', 18000), ('Tea', 9000);`

pairs.q: "Fill in a table name to build the query."
pairs.a: Type a name in the **Table name** field.

pairs.q: A database column name is empty or used more than once.
pairs.a: Give every included column a unique name (case-insensitive).

pairs.q: Invalid JSON at line X, column Y.
pairs.a: Fix the character at that position, or clean it up first with **JSON Formatter & Validator** in Developer Utilities.

data-server.title: Server Conversion
data-server.summary: Heavy conversions that cannot run in the browser: legacy spreadsheets (.xls/.ods/.xlsb) and tables from PDF. Processed on a server and paid with credits.

sections.heading: What it does
items: **Legacy spreadsheet → JSON (XLS/ODS/XLSB)**: reads .xls (Excel 97–2003), .ods (LibreOffice), or .xlsb.
**PDF table → JSON/Excel**: extracts tables from text-based PDFs. Scanned PDFs are not supported.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Choose the **Conversion type**, then pick a file. The file is validated in the browser before sending.
Choose the **Output format**: JSON, XLSX, or CSV.
Check the **Estimated cost**, press **Run conversion**, then confirm with **Run & download**. The result downloads automatically.
You can cancel while it runs; cancelling is not charged.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Spreadsheet input: `.xls`, `.ods`, `.xlsb`, max. **50 MB**. For .xlsx/.csv use Excel → JSON (free).
PDF input: `.pdf`, max. **30 MB**. Page count is estimated in the browser; the official count comes from the server.
File contents are checked (magic bytes): PDF must start with `%PDF`, .xls must be OLE2, .ods/.xlsb must be ZIP.

sections.heading: Limits & credit rules
sections.body: Both features can be paid straight from the balance without unlocking. Official prices always come from the server and are shown on the **Credits** page.
items: Legacy spreadsheet: **0.25 credits** (Rp250) per file; ×2 for files over 10 MB. Feature pack: 5 credits = 25 uses.
PDF table: **0.5 credits** (Rp500) per document; ×3 for 21–100 pages, ×6 above 100 pages. Feature pack: 5 credits = 12 uses.
Credits are only deducted after the server reports success. Failed or cancelled = free; retrying the same file is not charged twice.

pairs.a: You can still pick a file and see the estimate, but no file is sent and no credits are charged until the server is enabled.

pairs.q: "File contents do not match the extension" / "Not a valid PDF"
pairs.a: The file was probably renamed or is damaged. Re-save it from the original app.
Buy a credit package on the **Credits** page, then run again.
Wait a moment and try again.

sections.heading: How server conversion works
sections.body: Conversions are handled by the OneWebDev processing service through the app server.
items: File types are checked from their contents, not their names. Mismatched files are rejected at no cost.
Temporary files are deleted after success or failure, and results are delivered through signed, expiring links.
Credits are only deducted for successful conversions, once per request.

sections.heading: Tools & processing modes
items: **Browser only** (free): Image Converter, Find Colors at Image, Remove Image Metadata.
**Browser or server**: Remove Background, Image Upscaler, Video to Frames, Extract Audio. Browser mode is recommended.
**Server only** (plan quota): Video to GIF, Compress Video.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Open **All Media tools** for an overview, or pick a tool from the sidebar.
On two-mode tools, choose the **Processing mode**: browser or server.
Drop files on the upload area, set options, then run and download the results.
Server mode shows access status, balance, and a cost estimate before running.

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Image Converter: input PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, BMP, ICO, AVIF, SVG; output PNG, JPEG, WebP, or SVG (tracing). GIF/BMP/ICO/AVIF cannot be re-encoded and are saved as PNG.
Remove Background: transparent PNG output. Remove Image Metadata: lossless for JPEG/PNG/WebP; GIF/BMP/AVIF are re-encoded to PNG.

items: Remove Background: 0.5/image (pack 12×), ×1.5 above 10 MB, max. 25 MB.

sections.heading: How server mode works
sections.body: Server mode is handled by the OneWebDev processing service through the app server. Your browser never connects to the processing service directly.
items: Files go through a temporary upload link, are processed, then deleted automatically. Results are downloaded through signed, expiring links.
Progress is shown while processing. Failed, cancelled, or timed-out jobs are free.

page-maker.title: Page Designer (Page Maker)
page-maker.summary: A visual editor for designing one page from sections, Rows, and elements, then exporting its code to HTML, React, Vue, Svelte, or Angular.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body: One Page Maker design = one page. Designs can be grouped into a website in the **Website** menu.

sections.heading: How to use it
items: Page structure: **section** → **Row** → elements. Create a section from the preset picker first, then add Rows and elements.
Drag element cards onto the canvas or the **Structure** panel, or click **+**. Adjust the look in Settings.
Switch between **Design**, **Preview**, and **Code** modes; check Desktop, Tablet (768px), and Mobile (375px).
Save and open designs via **My Page Designs**. Undo with Ctrl+Z.

sections.heading: Code export
items: **Code** mode offers HTML, React, Vue, Svelte, and Angular. A single file downloads directly; several files download as a ZIP.
JavaScript events are written as the handler body (an `event` variable is available) and are included in exports; they run in Preview mode, not on the design canvas.

sections.heading: Limits & credit rules
items: Up to **10** saved page designs. When full, you are asked to delete old designs yourself — the app **never** deletes automatically.
**20** free exports. Re-exporting an identical result (same framework + content) and failed exports are not counted. After that a new export costs 5 credits.
**8** free section presets; the rest are premium (5–10 credits, one-time unlock).

Free elements include **Product Card**; Slider, Countdown, Progress Bar, Testimoni (testimonial), and Kartu Harga (pricing card) are premium (5–10 credits). Locked premium elements are left out of the output.
The **onClick** event is free; other events (onChange, onInput, onKeyDown, etc.) are premium (5 credits per event).

pairs.a: Delete old designs in that dialog, then press **Continue**. Designs used by a website folder show a warning before deletion.

sections.heading: Export output

vr.title: 360° Tour (VR)
vr.summary: Build a virtual tour from 360° panorama photos: move between rooms with hotspots, add info, images and audio, then download it as an HTML site that runs in browsers and VR headsets.

sections.heading: Purpose
items: A **tour** holds several **scenes** (one panorama photo each).
**Hotspots** are placed directly on the panorama: *Go to scene*, *Info* (text), *Image* or *Audio*.
The export uses **A-Frame 1.6.0** from the jsDelivr CDN. Its link is added to the `<head>` of index.html automatically.

sections.heading: How to use
items: Open **VR → 360° Tour**, name the tour, then **Create tour**.
Pick a scene and upload a panorama photo (drag onto the upload box or click).
In **Place hotspots** mode, choose a hotspot type and click a spot on the panorama. Set its label, target scene, text or file in the right panel.
Use **Try the tour** mode to test it like a visitor.
Click **Download tour (.zip)**. Upload the zip contents to hosting, or run a local server (see README.md inside the zip).

sections.heading: Input & output formats
items: Panorama: equirectangular JPG, PNG or WebP with a **2:1** ratio (e.g. 6000×3000), max **25 MB**.

File types are checked from their content, not the file name.

sections.heading: Limits & credits
items: **Free**: up to 3 scenes per tour, *Go to scene* & *Info* hotspots, HTML export.

guide.title: Website Builder Guide
guide.intro: How to build websites with Page Maker — from preparing icons and fonts, assembling pages from built-in elements or templates, to taking the code.

settings.title: Global Settings
settings.text: Prepare the icons and fonts your pages will use.

pageMaker.title: Page Designer (Page Maker)
pageMaker.text: Build Section → Row → built-in Elements, set backgrounds & events — or start from a template.

website.title: Build Full Website

alur.intro: Website Builder uses **one builder**: Page Maker. Prepare icons and fonts in Global Settings, then assemble pages from the built-in elements — or start from one of the **Website Templates**.
items: Everything you save (pages, icons, fonts) is stored **in this browser** (localStorage). It does not follow you to another browser or device.
Preview and code come from **the same engine**, so the code you download always matches what you see in the preview.
Code is available in five flavors: **HTML, React, Vue, Svelte, Angular**.
Page Maker stores **up to {{maxDesigns}} page designs**. When it's full, delete old designs yourself — the app never deletes designs automatically.

gs.intro: Where you prepare assets used in Page Maker. Open it from **Website Builder → Global Settings**. There are two tabs: **Icons** and **Fonts**.
iconSteps: Open the **Icons** tab, then click **Upload .svg** (several files at once, max. 200 KB each) or **Paste SVG code**.
When pasting code: enter an icon name, paste code that starts with `<svg` and ends with `</svg>`, check the preview, then click **Save icon**.
Hover over an icon to rename or delete it.
gs.iconsUse: Saved icons appear in the **Icon** group of an element's settings panel (Button, Card, Badge, and more). There you can set the position, size, spacing, and whether the icon follows the text color.
gs.iconDeleteTitle: Deleting an icon that is in use
gs.iconDeleteText: Elements that use it stay, but are shown without an icon.

head: Source
What you enter
Notes
rows: Type it exactly as on fonts.google.com (e.g. `Poppins`, `Playfair Display`). Quick suggestion buttons are available.
URL of a `.woff2/.woff/.ttf/.otf` file or a CSS stylesheet. Must be `https://` or a path from the site root (`/fonts/brand.woff2`). One file = one weight.

fontSteps: Open the **Fonts** tab, choose a source, enter the name, pick a **fallback font** (used while the font loads), then click **Add to library**.
Watch the status on the font card: **Loaded** means it's ready; **Failed to load** usually means a typo in the name or a URL that can't be opened.
For Google fonts, click the weight numbers on the card to add or remove loaded weights (at least one).
gs.baseText: The **Page base font** card in the Fonts tab sets the main font. It is used as the root font in **Page Maker** (and written into the exported code). Elements that choose their own font are not affected.
gs.useText: In the **Typography** panel, choose a **Font**: **Inherit** (from the parent, default), a font from your library, or a system font. It's currently available on Text, Button, Badge, Alert, and Anchor; other elements inherit the font from their parent. Exported code automatically includes `@import` or `@font-face` only for fonts that are actually used.
gs.renameText: Elements store the font as CSS text (e.g. `"Poppins", sans-serif`). To change a font, delete it and add it again with the new name. Elements using a deleted font fall back to the fallback font.

pm.intro: A visual builder for full pages. The canvas uses 100% of the screen width with no permanent sidebar; all settings open as popups. Use **Exit** in the top-left corner to return to the app.
pm.ruleText: Pages are nested: **Section → Row → Element**. A section is a full-width band with **normal (block)** layout — not flex. It contains **Rows**, and elements always live **inside a Row**. You can add **20 free built-in elements** (Button, Text, Image, Card, Product Card, Input, Tabs, Code, Menu, and more) plus **5 premium elements** (Slider, Countdown, Progress Bar, Testimonial, Pricing Card) that need credits. Sections and Rows can't be nested in themselves. A new page starts empty and asks you to pick the first section.
pm.ruleRow: Column layout lives on the **Row** (stack, row, or grid), not on the section. If you drop an element straight onto a section, a Row is created for it automatically.
pm.presetsText: The preset picker has two clear groups: **Free** (use right away) and **Premium** (lock icon, {{presetCost}} credits per preset, unlocked once).

head: Group
Presets
rows: Single Column, Centered Hero, Two-Column Hero, 3-Column Features, Content + Side, CTA Banner, Navbar, 4-Column Footer

Image Hero, Gradient Hero, 4-Column Stats, 3-Card Pricing, 3-Card Testimonials, 4-Column Team, Logo Strip, Two-Column FAQ, Newsletter, 4-Step Process, 3×2 Gallery, Two-Column Contact, 3-Card Articles, Dark Banner

pm.presetsNote: Each preset contains Rows with empty columns — you fill them in.
fillSteps: Click the **(+)** button in the middle of an empty column, or **Add** in the top bar. The **Add** popup opens with the **Elements**, **Groups**, and **Row** tabs.
**Click** an item to insert it at the current selection, or **drag** it onto the canvas — a marker line shows where it will land. The popup stays open, so you can add several items in a row.
The **Elements** tab holds the built-in elements. After adding one, change its look in **Settings**. The **Groups** tab holds small containers for arranging several elements inside a Row.
To add a new section, use the **(+)** button between two sections.
pm.plusTitle: The (+) buttons on elements and Rows
plusItems: **(+) on an element** (green circle on its bottom edge, or in the toolbar): adds a new element **right below** it, in the same Row.
**(+) on a Row** (purple circle on the Row's bottom edge, or in the toolbar): adds a **new Row right below** it. Other variants (2/3/4 columns, inline) are in the **Row** tab of the Add popup.
In the section toolbar, **(+)** adds a Row at the end of the section.
pm.rowStyleText: Select the Row (click an element inside it, then **Select parent**, or use the **Structure** panel) and open **Settings**: layout, gap, alignment, size, padding, background, border, radius, and shadow — like any other container.
pm.rowWidthText: **Row width** (Size & Spacing group) controls how wide the Row is inside the section:

head: Option
Result
rows: The Row is limited to the section's **Content width** (e.g. 1120px) and centered — about 80% on wide screens
The Row is 80% of the section area, centered
The Row fills the **whole** section area (minus the section's side padding). For true edge-to-edge, set the section's side padding to 0
Your own value in `px` or `%`; never wider than the section

pm.rowWidthNote: The same setting applies to the canvas, preview, and every export. On small screens the Row still shrinks with the screen.
pm.settingsText: Click a node on the canvas — an outline and the **node toolbar** appear: drag, settings, add (+), move up/down, duplicate, select parent, delete. The settings icon opens the **Settings** popup with style groups (content, size, typography, background, border, and more). Sections also have a **Section** group:

head: Setting
Purpose
rows: Maximum content width; the background still spans the page
Color, gradient, or image — see the Background section
Content arrangement: normal (block) for sections; stack, row, or grid for Rows

pm.pageSettings: The **Page** button (settings icon in the top bar) opens the whole-page settings, including the page class name.
modesItems: **Structure**: a tree of the whole page with drag-and-drop to move or reorder.

**My Page Designs**: save, open, or delete page designs. Up to **{{maxDesigns}} designs** can be stored — every design counts, including ones created from templates. Updating an existing design doesn't add to the count.
**Desktop** / **Tablet (768px)** / **Mobile (375px)** viewports: the canvas actually narrows, so responsive rules kick in (e.g. a grid becomes one column on Mobile).
**Design** mode (building, with overlays), **Preview** (no overlays, interactive), **Code** (preview on the left, code on the right).

[[Delete]] removes the selected node and shows an undo button; [[Esc]] clears the selection or closes a popup; [[Ctrl]]+[[Z]] / [[Ctrl]]+[[Shift]]+[[Z]] for Undo/Redo — even when focus is inside the canvas.
Popups can be dragged and their position is remembered. On screens below 640px they become bottom sheets.
pm.limitText: Once you have {{maxDesigns}} designs, new ones (including pages from a template) can't be saved until you delete old designs in **My Page Designs**. The app **never** deletes designs automatically — you choose what to remove.

bg.intro: Background settings are available on **sections, Rows, groups** (the **Background & Border** group) and on elements that have a background (Button, Text, Anchor, Alert, Badge, Icon, Card, List, Breadcrumbs; Input and Select are limited to color/gradient).

head: Type
Options
rows: Transparent — no background is written to the CSS
Linear (with angle) or radial, two colors + an optional middle color
URL (https:// or /path) or an uploaded image (max. 1.5 MB), cover/contain/original size, position, repeat, parallax, base color, and a transparent color overlay

bg.uploadTitle: Uploaded images are stored in the page
bg.uploadText: Uploaded images are stored as data URLs inside the design and the exported code. For large images, use a URL from your own hosting instead.

js.intro: The per-element **JavaScript (Event)** panel has been removed. Extra JavaScript is written **in full** under **Advanced → Custom JavaScript** on an element or section. The `element` variable (this element) and the `on(target, event, fn)` function are available.
items: Write complete code, including attaching events: `on(element, "click", function (event) { … })`. Listeners attached with `on` are removed automatically.
Code runs in **Preview** mode and in exports, not on the **Design** canvas (clicks there select elements).
Older designs with events are moved to Custom JavaScript automatically when opened, so they behave the same.
Code with syntax errors is marked red and left out of the output until fixed.

adv.intro: Every section, Row, and element has an **Advanced** group in Settings (free):

head: Setting
Details
rows: Unique on the page (starts with a letter). Duplicate IDs get -2, -3 suffixes automatically in the code, with a warning.
One or more classes separated by spaces; invalid classes are ignored.
Without braces = styles for that node. `&` = the node itself; other selectors are automatically scoped to inside the node, so they don't leak to other elements.
A function body with `element`, `elements`, `on(target, event, fn)`, `onCleanup(fn)`, `root`.

items: Custom JS runs **once** when the page loads, in **Preview** mode (isolated iframe) and in the export — not on the design canvas. Re-renders clean up the previous initialization first, so listeners don't pile up.
Errors are caught per node (logged to the console) and don't stop other nodes' code.

In exports: HTML calls `initCustomCode(document)` in `script.js`; React uses `useEffect`, Vue `onMounted/onBeforeUnmount`, Svelte `onMount`, Angular `ngAfterViewInit/ngOnDestroy`, all from `customCode.js` / `custom-code.ts`.
Custom CSS is written as pre-scoped global CSS (Vue: a non-scoped `<style>` block, Svelte: `:global()`, Angular: `ViewEncapsulation.None`) so it also applies inside child components.

code.intro: The **Code** element accepts **raw HTML**, CSS, and JavaScript (separate tabs, with syntax highlighting). CSS automatically applies only inside that element; JavaScript uses the same mechanism as Custom JS.
items: `<script>` tags in the HTML are removed (not executed) — move that code to the JavaScript tab.
In frameworks, the HTML is inserted as a string: React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, Vue `v-html`, Svelte `{@html}`, Angular `[innerHTML]` with `bypassSecurityTrustHtml`.
**Limitation:** React/Vue/Svelte/Angular components (JSX, SFC) can't be pasted — their syntax is shown as plain HTML.

menu.intro: **Menu** (Navigation group) builds website navigation automatically from the pages in a **website folder**. Item text = the current design name (or the **menu label** you set in the folder); link = the page **slug**, not the raw design name.
items: **Page source:** pick a folder, or leave it on **Automatic** — it uses the folder containing this page, or the first folder. Without a folder, the menu shows sample items (Home/About/Contact).
Turn off **All pages** to choose which pages are shown. The order follows the folder order.
Pages that are added, renamed, or removed show up in the menu immediately — folders only store design IDs.
Styling: horizontal/vertical, alignment, item spacing, text size & weight, padding, text/hover/active colors, active-page indicator, and vertical stacking on mobile.

site.intro: **One Page Maker design = one page** (Home, About, Contact…). **One folder = one website** with several pages (max. 50). Folders only store **references** (design ID + slug), so designs aren't duplicated and design changes carry over immediately. You get **{{freeSites}} free website folders**; more are unlocked with credits ({{siteSlotCost}} credits per extra slot).
steps: Create and save each page in Page Maker (My Page Designs) — or start from **Website Templates**.
Open **Website** (Website Builder menu) and create a new folder. Once the {{freeSites}} free folders are used, folder {{nextSite}} and beyond need an extra slot ({{siteSlotCost}} credits per slot).
Click **Add** on a saved design to put it in the folder.
Set the order (arrows), choose the **homepage**, edit the **slug** and **menu label**, swap a page's design, or remove a page.
Add a **Menu** element to your pages (the edit icon opens the design in Page Maker).
**Preview** the website: click menu links to move between pages. Then export from the **Code** tab.
items: Removing a page from a folder or deleting a folder does **not** delete the source design.
Slugs: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; unique per website; `index`, `assets`, `src`, `app`, `pages` are reserved. The initial slug comes from the design name (`About Us!` → `about-us`).
Deleted designs are flagged in the folder and skipped during preview/export (with a warning).
Old **Page Composer** data is safe: it appears in its own section on the Website page and can be converted into a single page design.
exportItems: React/Vue/Angular use clean URLs (`/about`); the server needs an **SPA fallback** to `index.html`. Svelte uses `#/about`, so no server configuration is needed.
Each page's styles, IDs, classes, Custom CSS/JS, backgrounds, and Code Elements are kept; each page's classes get a `page-slug` prefix so they don't clash.
Required packages (e.g. `react-router-dom`, `vue-router`) are listed in the README inside the zip.

tpl.intro: The **Website Templates** page (Website Builder menu) has {{templates}} ready-made website templates across many categories, each with 1–10 pages. **Free** templates can be used right away; **premium** templates are bought with credits and their price rises with page count and content quality. Every template can be previewed at no cost.

head: Tier
Preview
Download & edit
rows: Bought once: **15 credits per page + a 0–10 quality bonus** (20–160 credits, Rp20k–Rp160k); then download and edit any time at no extra cost

steps: Open **Website Templates**, filter by category, then click a template to preview it (Desktop/Tablet/Mobile).
**Download**: get the template as a **static HTML zip** (ready to upload to any host).
**Edit**: the template opens as a **new website folder** in Page Maker — each of its pages becomes a design you can change, then export like any other website.
items: Editing a template creates your own copy; the original template doesn't change, and you can create a new copy any time.
Creating a website folder from a template uses one website slot. If the {{freeSites}} free folders are taken, you'll be asked to unlock an extra slot ({{siteSlotCost}} credits).
tpl.quotaText: Every template page opened in Page Maker becomes a design and counts toward the **{{maxDesigns}}-design** limit. If there isn't enough room, delete old designs in **My Page Designs** first — nothing is deleted automatically.

head: Feature
Free
With credits
rows: 20 built-in elements (including Menu and Product Card)
Slider, Countdown, Progress Bar, Testimonial, Pricing Card: {{elementCost}} credits each (unlocked once)
Max. {{maxDesigns}} designs (all designs, including from templates; updates don't count)
— (can't be raised; delete old designs when full)
{{freeExports}} successful exports per account in Page Design (tracked on the server); exports from Full Website Builder are free and unlimited
Advanced (ID, Class, Custom CSS/JS), Code Element, Menu, website preview

credit.text: When you reach a limit or pick a premium feature, a dialog explains the credit cost. Premium items you've unlocked stay unlocked — you don't pay again.
credit.buy: Credits are bought on the **Credits** page (`/credits`). One balance covers every paid feature: Media & Data server features, premium templates, and premium Website Builder items.

example.title: Example: building a landing page
example.intro: The full flow from scratch, about 10 minutes (or start from the free company profile template in **Website Templates**):
steps: **Global Settings → Fonts:** add `Poppins` (Google Fonts, weights 400 and 700), wait for the **Loaded** status, then make it the **Page base font**. In the **Icons** tab, upload a few icons (e.g. arrow, check mark).
**Page Maker:** pick **Navbar** as the first section, then add **Centered Hero**, **3-Column Features**, **CTA Banner**, and **4-Column Footer** with the (+) buttons between sections.
Fill the Hero with **Text** (heading, Font: Poppins 700) and a **Button** (brand color, arrow icon). Fill each feature column with a **Card**.
Select the Hero section → **Background & Border** → **Image**, enter an image URL, and turn on a 40% overlay so the text stays readable.
Check **Tablet** and **Mobile**, and try the button in **Preview** mode.
Save the page in **My Page Designs**, then open **Code** mode, pick a framework, and download the `.zip`.

head: Framework
Output
rows: `index.html`, `style.css`, and `script.js` when there are interactive elements
A `.jsx` component + `.css`; stateful elements (Tabs, etc.) become child components

export.quota: In **Code** mode, each file is shown only **partially** (preview). The full code comes from the **Download** button: **{{freeExports}} successful exports** per account are free, then {{exportCost}} credit per export. One export = one successfully generated file (a zip or a single file). Re-downloading exactly the same output doesn't count; another framework counts as a new export; failed exports don't use your quota. Downloads from the **Full Website Builder** are free and unlimited.
export.names: File and component names follow the class name (`custom-page` becomes `CustomPage`). Example of using a React export in your project:
items: Classes follow the class name you set, with stable suffixes for inner parts (e.g. `custom-page__text-1`), so the CSS doesn't change when elements move.
Library fonts in use are included in the CSS (`@import` / `@font-face`) — no need to add them yourself.
Icons are inlined as SVG in the markup, so there are no extra image files.
export.backupText: Designs, icons, and fonts live in the browser's localStorage. Clearing site data, using private mode, or switching browsers loses them. Download the code (.zip) of finished work.

head: Problem
Cause and fix
rows: Check the spelling of the Google Font name or the file URL. Make sure the URL is https:// and opens directly in the browser.
Add it first in Global Settings → Icons. The code must start with `<svg` and end with `</svg>`.
Can't drop an element straight onto the page
By design: create a section first (Page Maker), then fill it with the (+) button.
Event doesn't run when clicked on the canvas
By design: in Design mode a click selects the element. Try it in Preview mode.
You picked a premium preset/event/element/template, created more than the {{freeSites}} free website folders, or used up the free export quota. Credits are bought on the Credits page.
A new design can't be saved
The {{maxDesigns}}-design limit is reached (template pages included). Delete old designs in My Page Designs; the app never deletes anything automatically.
Press [[Ctrl]]+[[Z]] or the undo button that appears after deleting.
A saved page doesn't show up
Make sure you pressed Save in My Page Designs. Pages are stored per browser.
It looks different on my site
Components inherit fonts from your site. Make sure the site's base font matches, or set the font directly on the element.

tips.habitTitle: A habit that speeds things up
tips.habitText: Get one element just right (e.g. the main button), then use **Duplicate** in the toolbar to copy it elsewhere — its styles and events are copied too.

lib.intro: The **Element → Library** menu adds popular JavaScript/CSS libraries to a page. Libraries load from a CDN (jsDelivr, pinned versions) in **Preview** and are included in the exported code automatically, so you never write the `<script>` tags yourself.

head: Library
Purpose
Attributes/classes in code
rows: Animates elements as they scroll into view
Ready-made CSS animations on page load
Charts for the **Chart** element (Data) — installed automatically, no Install button

steps: Click [[+ Add]], open the **Library** tab, then click **Add** on the library you want.
Select an element or group, open **Settings → Library (animation & effects)**, tick the library, then set the effect, duration and delay.
Open **Preview** to see the effect. Effects are off in edit mode so elements stay visible while you build.
items: HTML exports add the `<link>` tag in `<head>` and the `<script>` + init before `</body>`, only for libraries in use.

The **Chart** element (Element tab → Data) uses Chart.js. As soon as it is on a page, the Chart.js CDN link is added automatically to the exported HTML `<head>` and to LIBRARIES.md; the chart also renders live on the Design canvas.
React, Vue, Svelte and Angular exports include a **LIBRARIES.md** file with the CDN tags and `npm i` command. In single-page apps, re-run the init after components render.
**Remove** a library in the Library tab to drop it from the page; element effect settings are ignored while the library is not installed.
Premium templates use these libraries too. The list appears on each template's detail page (**Libraries used**).

hub.chipBrowser: Browser: free, files are not uploaded

connection.browser: Only needed to open the page (and to download AI models the first time). Subsequent processing can run offline.
connection.server: Required during upload, processing and result download.

cost.browser: Almost zero per job: only static hosting/CDN.
cost.server: Cost per job (CPU/GPU), temporary storage and egress bandwidth — grows with the number of jobs.

fileSize.browser: Limited by tab memory and Canvas limits (Safari/iOS about 16.7 MP). We cap each tool at 20–300 MB.
fileSize.server: Can be much larger (e.g. 2 GB videos), limited by upload, duration and cost policies.

formats.browser: Only what the browser can decode/encode: HEIC & TIFF usually cannot be read, AVIF cannot be encoded via Canvas, video codecs are limited (HEVC/ProRes often fail).

performance.browser: No upload/download time. Speed depends on the user's device (CPU, GPU/WebGPU). AI models are downloaded once on first use.
performance.server: Transfer time applies: a 20 MB file on a 10 Mbps connection needs about 16 seconds just to upload (20 × 8 ÷ 10), plus queueing. Processing on dedicated GPUs is consistent.

privacy.browser: Files never leave the device. Suitable for personal photos, documents and sensitive data.
privacy.server: Files are sent over HTTPS, stored temporarily, and must then be deleted. Requires a retention policy, access control and expiring result URLs.

quality.browser: Equivalent for PNG/JPEG/WebP conversion. AI models must be small/quantized to fit in the browser; built-in encoders cannot be tuned further.
quality.server: Full AI models, tunable encoders (mozjpeg, libavif), and frame-exact video extraction with FFmpeg.

resources.browser: Uses the user's device. One Canvas needs width × height × 4 bytes — a 24 MP photo is about 96 MB per copy, so phones can run out of memory.
resources.server: Uses our machines; can use large GPUs and tens of GB of RAM, but every job consumes paid capacity.

scalability.browser: Scales automatically: every user brings their own computing power.
scalability.server: Needs queues, autoscaling, rate limiting and monitoring as users grow.

hub.comparisonDescription: A comparison based on how each method works.
hub.description: Process images and videos right in your browser — free and private. For jobs that need large AI models or special codecs, a server mode with credit quotas is available.
hub.metaDescription: Media tools: image conversion, colors, background removal, video to frames, upscaler, and metadata removal.
hub.pricingDescription: Media server features use your plan's monthly quota (there is a Free plan).
hub.pricingNote1: Runs and video minutes renew every month.
hub.pricingNote2: Quota is only used when processing succeeds; failed/cancelled are free.

imageConverter.emptyText: Add PNG, JPG, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL, GIF, BMP, ICO, TIFF, QOI, or SVG. Everything is processed on your device with WebAssembly; nothing is uploaded.

deploy.tokenHint: The token goes straight from this browser to GitHub and is never sent to the OneWebDev server. It needs the public_repo scope.
deploy.remember: Remember the token while this tab is open
deploy.repoHint: If the repo doesn't exist it's created as a public repo. If it exists, its contents are replaced with this website.
deploy.doneCreated: Repo {{repo}} created and the website pushed.
deploy.pagesWait: GitHub Pages takes about 1–2 minutes before the address below opens.
deploy.vercelHint: Vercel asks you to sign in and then imports this repo. No extra settings: the HTML website just works, and every later deploy to this repo updates Vercel as well.
deploy.redeployHint: To update the website, press Deploy again with the same repo name.

errors.token: The GitHub token is invalid or expired.
errors.scope: The token lacks permissions. Create a token with the public_repo scope (or Contents, Pages and Administration for a fine-grained token).
errors.rateLimit: GitHub rate limit reached. Try again in a few minutes.
errors.repoName: That repo name can't be used (it may belong to a private repo or another organisation).
errors.notOwner: This token has no write access to that repo.
errors.network: Can't reach GitHub. Check your internet connection.
errors.pages: Files were pushed, but GitHub Pages couldn't be turned on. Enable it in Settings → Pages (main branch, /root folder).
errors.files: The website files couldn't be prepared. Try again.
errors.blocked: Free export quota used up. Once the credit payment is approved, the deploy runs automatically.

deploy.lastHint: Deploying again updates the same repo, so the site address stays the same.
